requests.title: AI-assisted clothing and accessories design, from idea to factory and store
requests.ask: AI agent assisted, software assisted clothing design, where the software handles basically everything including marketing, distribution, manufacturing and manufacturer deals. The designer works in a web browser (and later VR) by voice and by pointing and clicking: describe the garment, get a rendering, give spoken or manual feedback, compare versions. Fabric choices come from what manufacturers offer, with prices, so the designer knows what each shirt costs. From an interview with a designer planning a unisex line with raised, '3D' prints of classical and devotional paintings, sold in Europe and the US, possibly with other brands on the same site for a commission. A second interview added: sunglasses with the brand's logo on the frame and case, starting from a stock frame a manufacturer makes, with the measurements chosen (they estimated about 20 euros to make and 60 to 70 to sell); full-wardrobe sets, started small and limited, with pricing tiers that change fabric quality, and fitted to the target audience (age band, gender, style, climate, season); pieces both in-house and from other brands; and trying garments on virtually, by AI or AR.
requests.next: Live: the studio (voice/typed and drag design, three alternatives, costing, tech pack, quote request, launch kit), a sunglasses designer (stock frame, size, logos, case, cost, quote request with the EU/US test reports) and a wardrobe planner (capsule for an audience, outfit count, in-house vs partner pieces, first drop within a budget). Unproven: whether the designer gets a real garment or pair quoted with it. Next: their artwork and real quotes through it; colour separation from an uploaded painting landed 2026-11-03 (inks, screen count, thin-line warnings, raised outline, films; unproven on a real painting through a printer); a WebGL 3D garment with the artwork mapped on and drag-to-orbit landed 2026-11-04 (a rounded solid, no drape or fit); a size finder and size run (ease per size from chest/waist/hip/height; a split of the order by the audience's chest curve; typical chart, replaceable by the factory's) landed 2026-11-04; a front-view try-on of the recommended size over a body drawn from the shopper's measurements (ease at chest, waist and hem, where the hem lands) landed 2026-11-04; a one-ink halftone film from the separation (dot size by region lightness, mesh check) on the page 2026-11-04; the size run costed with cloth by size, metres to buy and blended cost per piece on the page 2026-11-05 (area rule, not a marker); partner-brand commission and a settlement statement with refunds on the page 2026-11-05 (hand-worked numbers, no real brand yet); a cutting plan from pattern pieces packed on the fabric width (lays, plies, spares; rectangles, so cautious against CAD) on the page 2026-11-05; each lay drawn to scale with a cut-ticket CSV on the page 2026-11-05; a pre-order planner (orders and visitors to reach the factory minimum, chance of funding, loss if not) on the page 2026-11-05; then VR, camera try-on, sleeves (ROADMAP.md). Import duty by destination (US/EU/UK customs value, extra tariff, zero-duty origin with proof, import VAT apart; rates typed from memory, unchecked) landed 2026-11-06; the cost sheet fills its duty percent from market and origin 2026-11-06; single-parcel duty (EU flat 3 under 150 from July 2026, US no threshold, UK) landed 2026-11-06. US sales tax nexus by state (thresholds, and/or rules, planned crossing; 24 states typed from memory, unchecked) landed 2026-11-06. A measurement spec (points of measure with tolerances by size, in the tech pack) and a pass/fail check of a factory sample landed 2026-11-07 (typical tolerances, no real sample yet). Photo and live-camera try-on from two shoulder taps (camera.html, scale from shoulder span; no pose model, no real photo yet) landed 2026-11-07. Final-inspection sampling (sample size, accept number, chance of passing, verdict with the worst defect rate hidden) landed 2026-11-07; exact maths, no real inspection report yet. A partner brand's product CSV checked, priced for brand payout and shop take, and built into a multi-brand shop page landed 2026-11-07 (partnerfeed.mjs; no real partner feed yet). GTIN-13 barcodes per style, colour and size from the brand's own GS1 prefix (check digit, reserved-range warning, EAN-13 SVG, label sheet, CSV) landed 2026-11-07; decoded by an independent reader, not scanned from a printed label. A production timeline (latest start for an on-sale date, or earliest on-sale date from a start, over sample rounds, production, freight and customs, with factory closure windows and a delay allowance; timeline.html) landed 2026-11-08 (stage lengths and the Lunar New Year window are unchecked assumptions). A cart for payment-link shops (one checkout per piece) landed 2026-11-08. A worked sunglasses profit page (20 euros made, 65 sold: 20.96 per order at 12% returns, so at most that to win a customer) landed 2026-11-08, recomputed by test from returns.mjs; placeholder inputs, duty rate from memory. A factory run vs print-on-demand comparison (pod.html: expected profit of each and of a run plus print-on-demand overflow under Poisson demand, best run size, crossover demand) landed 2026-11-08; placeholder prices, no real designer's numbers. A price-test calculator (pricepoint.html: elasticity from two observed prices and sales, best shelf price after VAT and fees, sensitivity to the elasticity guess) landed 2026-11-08; placeholder inputs, no real price test. A green-claims checker (greenclaims.html: product copy scanned for generic environmental words, offset-based neutrality claims, own badges, future promises, legal requirements sold as features and unproven recycled or organic wording, with safer wording; rules read from Directive (EU) 2024/825, applying from 27 September 2026; short English phrase list, not legal advice, no real brand's copy run through it) landed 2026-11-09. A colour approval check (colour.html: CIEDE2000 of a lab dip or printed swatch against the target, pass/fail per colour, note to the factory; formula pinned on published test pairs, no real lab dip yet) landed 2026-11-09. Automatic shoulder finding for the camera try-on (pose.mjs, an on-device MediaPipe pose model loaded on click; the picture stays on the device) landed 2026-11-10; one real photo run, no tape-measured photo yet. A painting finder (artwork.html: Art Institute of Chicago and Met open-access search from the browser, public-domain works only, pixels-per-inch verdict at the print width and method, hand-off to the studio, which now keeps the original's pixel size and warns when a print outgrows it) landed 2026-11-11; tested on documented API shapes with the APIs mocked, not yet against a live search. Live tracking on the camera stream ("Follow me live", a One Euro filter over the pose model on video frames, about 15 a second) landed 2026-11-11; tuned on synthetic frames only, no real person on a webcam yet. Index separation for paintings (indexsep.mjs, the studio page's "Index separation" button: the flat inks as square dots by error diffusion) landed 2026-11-11: on nine real public-domain paintings it sat closer to the painting than flat inks from 1 m on 8 of 9 (rough eye-blur measure); no real printer has printed one yet. Dot gain for the index separation (a spread model with later inks over earlier ones, model-based error diffusion that compensates for a set gain, a calibration strip and a gain read-back from a photo of the proof) landed 2026-11-11: a grey ramp at 20% gain went from 3.39 to 0.78 delta E; on the nine paintings it moved the print only 0.1-0.26 because the inks' colour range dominates, and a guess too high was worse than none; no real proof yet. A search over the piece order for the nesting marker (swap or move pieces, keep when no longer; a placer about 10x faster with the same answers) landed 2026-11-12: 2-5% shorter markers on tee, crewneck and hoodie runs, none on long sleeves; off-grain tilt tried and not shipped; no factory marker compared yet.
